articles.title: Packers make $92M Tucker Kraft contract decision that can smash NFL record
articles.summary: This massive new contract for Tucker Kraft is a major record-breaker.
articles.body:
The Green Bay Packers were approaching the 2026 season with the intention of signing Tucker Kraft to a long term deal. But, with only one day before their season opener, they were cutting it close.

Fortunately, the Packers got the deal done. According to ESPN's Adam Schefter , Kraft and the Packers have agreed to a massive $92 million four-year contract extension to keep the star tight end in Green Bay .

This major new deal for Kraft doesn't just keep him in Green Bay for the foreseeable future, it also smashed the current record for largest contract for a tight end, with second place not remotely close.

Packers smash TE contract record with $92M Tucker Kraft deal

"ESPN sources: Green Bay TE Tucker Kraft and the Packers reached agreement today on a four-year, $75 million extension worth up to $92 million that includes a $26.5 million signing bonus," Schefter reports.

While this four-year contract for Kraft is a $75 million deal, it has a chance of eclipsing $92 million overall depending on incentives he hits. Considering his talent, it's likely he'll climb well over that $75 million mark.

If Kraft earns the minimum of this $75 million extension, which isn't likely, his new deal is still going to be third-most among all tight ends, right behind George Kittle at $76.4 million and Trey McBride at $76 million.

On a per-year basis, Kraft's new deal is also third, coming in at $18.75 million per-year right behind Kittle ($19.1M) and McBride ($19M).

But if Kraft can reach his max value on his new deal, $92 million overall and $23M per-year, it'd easily clear the current record for tight ends.

While the floor of his contract isn't a record-breaker, so long as Kraft can meet some of his incentives, he'll clear the record-setting contract from Kittle at $76.4M and $19.1M per-year.

This is a very strong contract for Kraft, and while it might not be the $20M per-year deal he was seeking, so long as he hits some incentives, his goal of a record-breaking contract is well within reach.

articles.title: Loss of legal immigrant caregivers puts America’s seniors at risk
articles.summary: Every lapsed visa or expired protection is a resident who loses the person who knows their routines, care needs and potential risks best.
articles.body:
The quality of long-term care depends heavily on appropriate staffing levels and continuity of care, as residents fare best when they are routinely treated by the same trained caregivers who know their needs and notice warning signs.

Many documented instances of elder abuse and neglect trace back to facilities that either lacked sufficient staffing or could not maintain a stable, trained team over time. In fact, that pattern that shows up repeatedly in lawsuits involving vulnerable residents.

What often goes unspoken in these cases is the identity of the caregivers themselves. In skilled nursing homes and assisted living facilities across the country, a large share of the workforce providing hands-on care to aging residents is made up of legal immigrants, including visa-holders, green card-holders, naturalized citizens and workers who hold lawful humanitarian status such as temporary protected status.

That workforce is now shrinking. The elder care industry should move swiftly to address current and future staffing gaps — something it has been slow to address previously.

Roughly one in three home care workers and one in five nursing home workers are immigrants, according to research from Harvard, the Massachusetts Institute of Technology and the University of Rochester. The same research found that, when the immigrant population increases in a metro area, elderly mortality in long-term care facilities measurably declines. This is because a larger immigrant population expands the overall pool of available caregivers rather than displacing native-born workers from a fixed number of jobs.

Additional research analyzed by the Kaiser Family Foundation shows that immigrants make up about 30 percent of direct long-term care workers overall, and 41 percent of home health aides. Further, a significant rise in a given community’s immigrant population decreases the likelihood that an elderly person will be moved into an elder care facility at all, as immigrant caregivers often make it possible for older Americans to remain safely and receive care in their own homes.

When legal immigration pathways are disrupted, facilities lose trained staff overnight, and residents pay the price in broken continuity of care. In an interview with PBS , a senior care leader described facilities losing between 16 and 40 workers overnight when protections such as temporary protected status have lapsed. This occurred not because those workers had done anything wrong, but because their legal status expired and there was no pathway to renew or reapply.

A loss on that scale does not give a facility time to recruit and train replacements before the next shift. The immediate response is almost always for each staff member to absorb more residents, which is precisely the staffing dilution that is a common thread in elder abuse and neglect cases.

This is happening at a moment when the population needing care is growing faster than the workforce that provides them with care. It is pushing facilities toward a staffing crisis that the industry is poorly positioned to absorb. The fallout from these losses is systemic and devastating for the people caught in the middle, as care teams that residents had come to trust are broken apart and residents are forced to adjust to unfamiliar caregivers who do not yet know their needs or history.

Even skilled, well-trained caregivers become less effective under these conditions, because quality care depends on having enough time with each resident to understand their needs and potential risks, not just rely on credentials to do the job. This leaves facilities in a position where they must consider reducing the number of beds they can safely staff or, in some cases, close entire wings of facilities.

Legal immigration pathways are critical to the elder care infrastructure. Providing quality care to the seniors who depend on skilled nursing homes and assisted living facilities requires treating adequate staffing and continuity of care as a critical part of the elder care infrastructure.

Legal immigration pathways for healthcare workers deserve recognition as a necessity for care quality, not a peripheral policy debate. Every lapsed visa or expired protection is a resident who loses the person who knows their routines, care needs and potential risks best.

Lawmakers debating these pathways in the abstract are also, whether they realize it or not, deciding who answers the call button at 2 a.m. in long-term care facilities across the country. That decision will be felt in individual rooms, and by some of our nation’s most vulnerable individuals, long before it ever shows up in a policy report.

Edward Dudensing is the founder and lead counsel at Dudensing Law.

articles.title: Tiger Woods’ potential NEXUS Cup return comes after DUI case settlement, putting his golf comeback in focus
articles.summary: International Sports News: Tiger Woods could return to a golf course as early as Monday, September 14, when his annual NEXUS Cup begins at Liberty National Golf Club in New Jers.
articles.body: Tiger Woods could return to a golf course as early as Monday, September 14, when his annual NEXUS Cup begins at Liberty National Golf Club in New Jersey. The event would mark Woods’ first possible golf appearance since his March arrest and his first since settling the case on September 2. Woods has not played competitively since the 2024 Open Championship, making his presence at the two-day charity event worth watching.Tiger Woods could return to golf at NEXUS Cup after DUI caseThe 2026 NEXUS Cup is scheduled for September 14-15 at Liberty National, with Woods serving as the host. According to the NEXUS Cup’s official website, the invitation-only amateur event will bring together 18 foursomes, with proceeds going to the TGR Foundation.Woods is expected to be around the event, although there is no official confirmation that he will hit golf balls. Golf insider TWLEGION said on X that Woods could appear Monday and noted that he “typically gives a clinic” and could be seen hitting balls.The event guide shows golf beginning Monday morning, while Tuesday includes a golf Q&A featuring PGA Tour professionals. That gives Woods several chances to be around the game without taking part in a competitive tournament.His possible return comes less than two weeks after he ended the legal case linked to his March crash. On September 2, Woods pleaded no contest to a reduced reckless-driving charge in Martin County, Florida. The original DUI charge was reduced, and he also accepted a careless-driving citation.According to Reuters, Woods received a five-year driver’s license suspension and fines totaling $1,500. He avoided jail time. Judge Darren Steele also gave him a clear warning: “There are no exceptions. If you were to drive for any reason at all, you would go immediately back to jail.”Tiger Woods’ golf comeback remains uncertain after March arrestThe case began after Woods’ SUV crashed on Jupiter Island, Florida, on March 27. The vehicle struck a truck trailer while Woods was trying to pass it and rolled onto its side. No one was injured.Woods initially pleaded not guilty and later stepped away from golf while seeking treatment. He missed the Masters and has remained away from competitive play since the 2024 Open Championship.A return at the NEXUS Cup would not mean Woods is ready for PGA Tour competition. It would simply give fans a chance to see him with a club in his hands again.That distinction matters because Woods has dealt with major physical setbacks throughout his career. The 50-year-old has undergone several back surgeries and suffered serious leg injuries in his 2021 car crash. Yet he has repeatedly found ways to return.For now, the NEXUS Cup is the clearest upcoming setting for another one of those moments. articles.title: Kupcho borra la ventaja de Europa en la Solheim con dos putts memorables
articles.standfirst: La estadounidense asesta un duro golpe anímico a las de Nordqvist antes de los individuales
articles.summary: La estadounidense asesta un duro golpe anímico a las de Nordqvist antes de los individuales
articles.body: Europa se acostará este sábado preguntándose cómo es posible que la Solheim Cup llegue empatada a los partidos individuales del domingo. Después de dominar por 3-1 los foursomes de la mañana, de volver a disfrutar por la tarde de una pareja formidable formada por Maja Stark y Linn Grant y de asistir a una exhibición de Carlota Ciganda, autora de ocho birdies, el equipo de Anna Nordqvist vio cómo su ventaja se evaporaba en un desenlace difícil de digerir. Jennifer Kupcho, con dos putts memorables en los dos últimos hoyos, transformó lo que parecía encaminado hacia un 9-7 europeo en un 8-8 que deja todo por decidir en Bernardus. El primero de esos putts fue una auténtica barbaridad. Europa llegó al 17 uno arriba en el último partido, con Ciganda y Céline Boutier frente a Kupcho y Lindy Duncan, y las dos europeas pegaron dos segundos golpes extraordinarios. Boutier se dejó un par de metros para birdie y Carlota, tal vez un poquito más. Kupcho, que había tenido problemas por la derecha, parecía prácticamente descartada del hoyo. Todas las miradas iban hacia su compañera de partido. Pero entonces ocurrió lo que absolutamente nadie esperaba... Desde fuera del green, a casi 28 metros de la bandera, Kupcho embocó para birdie. Un putt de esos que cambian no sólo un hoyo, sino también la presión de todo lo que viene detrás. Lo que segundos antes eran dos oportunidades europeas para cerrar el partido se convirtieron de repente en dos putts para evitar perder el hoyo. Carlota falló por la izquierda. Boutier, por la derecha. Partido empatado y al 18, con un varapalo anímico enorme para la española y la francesa, que parecían tener el partido en el bolsillo hasta ese 'purazo' de la norteamericana. "Ha sido una locura", reconocería después la propia Kupcho. Su compañera fue todavía más gráfica. "Lo del 17 no lo olvidaré nunca", aseguró Duncan. Y todavía faltaba otro golpe. Boutier encontró el agua desde el tee del 18 y Carlota se marchó al rough de la derecha, aunque tuvo la fortuna de evitar un bunker con un talud complicadísimo. La navarra se lo pensó mucho antes de elegir un hierro 5 y ejecutar un magnífico golpe prácticamente ciego para alcanzar el green. Desde unos diez metros volvió a rozar el milagro: su putt para birdie pasó a centímetros del hoyo. Duncan falló su oportunidad. Pero no Kupcho. La estadounidense, que hasta esta tarde no había aportado un solo punto a su equipo, embocó otro putt de más de diez metros para birdie y desató la locura del combinado de las barras y estrellas. Victoria por uno arriba y empate a ocho antes de los individuales. Un desenlace especialmente cruel para Carlota, que había sostenido a Europa durante buena parte de la tarde con una exhibición en los greenes. La española firmó ocho birdies en 16 hoyos —3, 5, 6, 9, 10, 13, 14 y 16— y protagonizó algunos de los momentos de mayor comunión con las gradas. Su larguísimo birdie del 6, desde unos nueve metros y con una caída endiablada, fue uno de ellos. Y cuando Estados Unidos consiguió empatar el partido en el 12, respondió ganando inmediatamente el 13 y el 14 con otros dos birdies para colocar a Europa dos arriba. Ayer remontó para salvar medio punto. Hoy parecía ir a por la victoria. Sin duda, era el momento de romper el partido. Pero en el 15 llegó un error difícil de explicar. Boutier atacó demasiado la bandera del peligroso par tres y encontró el agua. Carlota, después de ver el golpe de su compañera y teniendo disponible la zona central del green, tomó prácticamente la misma línea y terminó también en el obstáculo. Un fallo estratégico importante. Estados Unidos ganó el hoyo con par. Europa mantuvo el uno arriba tras el 16 y llegó al 17 con el partido todavía en sus manos. Hasta que apareció Kupcho. Antes de ese final de película (de terror en este caso para las chicas de Nordqvist), Maja Stark y Linn Grant habían vuelto a demostrar que son una de las grandes fortalezas de este equipo europeo. Después de derrotar por la mañana 3&2 a Nelly Korda y Allisen Corpuz, hasta entonces invictas juntas en foursomes, las suecas se impusieron por la tarde 2&1 a Megan Khang y Lauren Coughlin. Stark abrió el partido de manera espectacular, embocando directamente su segundo golpe desde la calle para eagle en el 1, después de haber firmado también un eagle increíble por la mañana en el corto par 4 del 8. Pero Estados Unidos reaccionó y las suecas llegaron al 10 uno abajo. Ahí cambió el partido. Europa ganó consecutivamente el 11, 12 y 13. Grant embocó un gran birdie en el primero, dejó prácticamente dada su opción en el siguiente y Stark completó la secuencia con otro putt de unos seis metros. Incluso después de que Estados Unidos ganara el 16 tras mandar Stark su segundo golpe al agua, la sueca respondió como hacen las grandes jugadoras: birdie en el 17 desde tres metros para sellar el 2&1. "Sabes que Linn no está entrando en pánico y Linn sabe que yo tampoco. Eso te permite centrarte en ti misma", explicó después Stark. Grant resumió la reacción: "En los nueve segundos lo pusimos en marcha. Empezamos a jugar como queríamos". Su victoria tuvo además un enorme valor estadístico. Después de acabar por la mañana con la condición de invictas de Korda y Corpuz en foursomes, por la tarde las suecas pusieron fin a seis victorias consecutivas de Khang, a sus nueve partidos seguidos sin perder y al inicio invicto de Coughlin en la Solheim, que había disputado sus siete primeros encuentros con un balance de cinco victorias y dos empates. Stark y Grant se han convertido en las grandes romperrachas de Europa. No todo salió tan bien desde el banquillo europeo. Anna Nordqvist tomó dos decisiones importantes para los fourballs de la tarde y ninguna funcionó. La primera fue insistir con Charley Hull y Lottie Woad. Después de perder 6&5 por la mañana y de haber sumado sólo medio punto en sus tres primeros partidos, la capitana mantuvo juntas a sus dos estrellas, ambas entre las diez mejores del mundo. Se convirtieron así en la primera pareja que disputa unida las cuatro sesiones de parejas de una misma Solheim Cup. El resultado final ha sido contundente: ninguna victoria y medio punto de cuatro posibles (0-3-1). Hasta que diera comienzo esta Solheim, 40 jugadoras habían disputado las cuatro sesiones por parejas de una misma edición del torneo. En los 40 casos habían sumado al menos un punto en el total de esos cuatro partidos. Lauren Coughlin se incorpora a esa lista esta semana. Al igual que Hull y Woad, que tendrán el dudoso honor de ser las únicas de esa lista en no sumar al menos un punto (solo medio en cuatro partidos...). Lo cierto es que esta vez estuvieron mucho más cerca de ganar que en los tres intentos anteriores. Hull jugó su mejor golf de la semana, aunque varios putts se escaparon rozando el hoyo, y Woad mostró una enorme personalidad en el tramo final. La rookie ganó el 10, embocó un birdie bajo máxima presión para empatar el 15 y otro en el 17 para prolongar el partido. Pero en el 18, con Hull en el agua después de elegir precisamente una madera 3 para evitar ese peligro, Woad dejó corto su largo putt de birdie y Yealimi Noh y Andrea Lee ganaron uno arriba. Noh fue una pesadilla para las europeas, especialmente con su putter de 'escoba'. Su propia compañera reconoció después que nunca la había visto patear así. Y la decisión de Nordqvist de mantener a Hull y Woad juntas queda inevitablemente bajo el foco. La capitana parecía traer preparado antes del torneo un plan y decidió mantenerlo hasta el final fueran cuales fueran las circunstancias y los resultados de las primeras sesiones. Con esta pareja, no funcionó. Tampoco dio resultado romper una pareja que sí estaba funcionando. Mimi Rhodes y Nastasia Nadaud habían ganado juntas el viernes por la tarde (2&1) y el sábado por la mañana (4&3). Dos partidos, dos victorias. Sin embargo, Nordqvist decidió dar descanso a Rhodes pensando en los cruces individuales de mañana y emparejar a Nadaud con Leona Maguire. Otra apuesta fallida. Las europeas perdieron 3&2 frente a Rose Zhang y Auston Kim. Maguire intentó cambiar el partido con un espectacular eagle en el 8 y un birdie en el 9, reduciendo una desventaja de tres hoyos a sólo uno, pero las estadounidenses respondieron ganando consecutivamente el 10, 11 y 12. Nadaud todavía prolongó el encuentro con un magnífico birdie en el difícil 15, pero Zhang lo cerró en el 16. La paradoja es que Nordqvist decidió mantener una pareja que no estaba funcionando y separar otra que llevaba pleno de victorias. Y ambas apuestas terminaron en rojo. Europa había comenzado la tarde 7-5 después de su magnífico 3-1 matinal. Stark y Grant colocaron el octavo punto en el marcador, pero Estados Unidos ganó los otros tres fourballs siguientes para completar una reacción formidable y devolver la Solheim al punto de partida. El golpe fue especialmente duro en el último partido. Al terminar, Boutier rompió a llorar desconsoladamente. Julia López acudió inmediatamente a abrazarla. Poco después, las europeas formaron un corro cerrado alrededor de Nordqvist. La capitana tomó la palabra, dio consignas y trató de levantar los ánimos de sus jugadoras. No quedaba otra. Después de dos días, 16 partidos y una montaña rusa de emociones, Europa y Estados Unidos están exactamente donde empezaron: empatadas. Ahora le toca a las europeas romper otra estadística: la que sitúa a Estados Unidos por delante si solo se tienen en cuenta los puntos de los partidos individuales desde que empezó a disputarse la Solheim. Es hora de que Bernardus apriete al máximo. Después de un sábado con un desenlace increíble, llega la hora de la verdad en esta emocionante Solheim Cup que está dejando ya imágenes para la historia, como los dos putts 'kilométricos' de Kupcho para cambiar el optimismo de bando.

articles.title: Solheim Cup 2026: Charley Hull & Lottie Woad toil as Europe level with US heading into singles
articles.summary: Should Europe fail to reach the 14½ points they require to win the Solheim Cup on Sunday questions will surely be asked of captain Anna Nordqvist's faith in Charley Hull and Lottie Woad as a pairing.
articles.body:
Should Europe fail to reach the 14½ points they require to win the Solheim Cup on Sunday, questions will surely be asked of captain Anna Nordqvist's faith in Charley Hull and Lottie Woad as a pairing.

Europe's misfiring star pair were beaten in both of Saturday's sessions and have contributed just half a point from four matches to the scoreline of 8-8 as the contest heads into Sunday's decisive 12 singles matches.

Woad confirmed on Saturday evening that "Plan A" had always revolved around her and Hull featuring in all five matches, but with their struggles particularly evident on the greens it begs the question of why that strategy was not revisited.

"We didn't hole many putts in the morning and all afternoon, and that's the difference, really," Woad said.

"The people we played were holing 15-footers and we weren't."

"Just couldn't buy a putt," was Hull's summation of the day, before Woad added: "It doesn't matter who wins the points. I would happily lose my matches if we win."

But while there were few plaudits for the English duo, the irrepressible Swedish pairing of Maja Stark and Linn Grant led the charge for Nordqvist's team at Bernardus Golf Club in the Netherlands.

Having defeated the unbeaten US partnership of world number one Nelly Korda and Allisen Corpuz 3&2 in the morning foursomes, Stark and Grant fought back in wonderful fashion to triumph 2&1 against Megan Khang and the previously undefeated Lauren Coughlin in the afternoon fourballs.

Starting day two level at 2-2, the Swedes' opening point, against a Korda and Corpuz pairing that had won all five of their previous matches together, set the tone for Europe to win three points.

Mimi Rhodes and Nastasia Nadaud became the first rookie duo to win two matches in one edition of the biggest team competition in women's golf, while Leona Maguire and Esther Henseleit also delivered a point as Europe led 7-5.

Stark and Grant were sent out in the afternoon and delivered a third point of the week to maintain their 100% record at this year's event.

It was Khang's first loss for six matches and it delivered a wonderful boost to Nordqvist's team as the US challenge warmed up in the afternoon and threatened to overturn Europe's advantage.

However, Nordqvist's decision to persist with Hull and Woad will surely be placed under further scrutiny given the way events unfolded.

The pair, Europe's highest ranked players, had asked to play together this week.

But after they were summarily thrashed by Alison Lee and Coughlin in the foursomes - a Solheim Cup record equalling 6&5 defeat - the experiment of pairing the world number seven and eight together looked to have run its course.

Yet when Hull and Woad emerged together again to face Yealimi Noh and Andrea Lee, to almost universal surprise, Europe's captain defended her decision.

"I don't think people understand - these are the best players in the world," said a defiant Nordqvist.

"Lottie, herself, made six birdies in the afternoon [yesterday]. They are playing solid."

Unfortunately solid was not enough to prevail in the fourballs, particularly with Noh delivering a performance that included five birdies and an eagle on the front nine.

A Woad birdie on the 17th sent the match down the last with the English pair needing to win the hole to salvage half a point.

But for the second day running, Hull found water off the tee to immediately put pressure on Woad, and Noh and Lee held on for the win.

Woad also pointed out that their opponents in Friday's fourball and Saturday's foursomes matches just played better golf.

"In the fourball, we were 10, 11 under, and it was a great match," said the European rookie.

"And then I don't think anyone would have beaten who we played on Saturday morning. They were seven under through 14, so credit to them.

"Everyone's played amazing when we've played them. So, yeah, it's just matchplay, isn't it? You can play bad and win and play well and lose."

And the day ended with a huge momentum swing for the US.

Jennifer Kupcho holed a monster 91-foot putt on the 17th and followed it by dispatching another lengthy putt on the final hole to steal an unlikely point from the grasp of Carlota Ciganda and Celine Boutier who had been one up with four to play.

Just as Ciganda pilfered a half point in Friday's final match to give Europe the impetus coming into Saturday, so Kupcho's point will do likewise for the US, who need to reach 14 points on Sunday to retain the trophy.

articles.title: Solheim Cup 2026: Team USA pull level with Team Europe in fourballs after late Jennifer Kupcho magic at Bernardus Golf
articles.summary: Jennifer Kupcho found two late birdies to snatch victory for her and Lindy Duncan over Carlota Ciganda and Celine Boutier; Team USA won three points in fourballs to sit tied 8-8 with Team Europe heading into final day; watch the Sunday singles live from 9am on Sky Sports Golf
articles.body:
Anna Nordqvist's side tied both sessions on Friday before winning three of the four points on offer in the morning foursomes , giving them the advantage, only for Team USA to edge the afternoon fourballs and set up a thrilling final day.

Stark and Grant delivered again as they claimed an impressive 2&1 win over unbeaten duo Megan Khang and Lauren Coughlin, their third win in as many sessions together, as Hull and Woad fell to a final-hole loss to Yealimi Noh and Andrea Lee.

Hull and Woad are the first ever to play all four sessions in a Solheim Cup together but have returned just 0.5 points, with Rose Zhang and Auston Kim reducing the deficit further when they beat Leona Maguire and Nastasia Nadaud 3&2.

Carlota Ciganda snatched a dramatic half-point with the final putt of Friday's fourballs session and was taken to the 18th again in the bottom match, after a 90-foot birdie from Jennifer Kupcho at the par-four 17th pulled her and Lindy Duncan level.

Kupcho delivered more brilliance at the last, holing from over 20 feet to claim a 1up win over Ciganda and Celine Bouter and spark incredible celebrations on the final green.

That dramatic finish leaves Team USA requiring six points on the final day to retain the title, two years on from their home win in Virginia, while Team Europe would require a further 6.5 points for a first outright victory since 2021.

Late drama leaves Europe and USA tied again

The Swedish stars were sent out first again, having ended Nelly Korda and Allisen Corpuz's 100 per cent foursomes record earlier in the day, with Stark holing out from the first fairway to find her second eagle of the day.

Coughlin hit back with successive holes from the third, leaving Europe behind for the first time this week, then the two teams shared each hole until Grant won the 11th and 12th with birdies.

Stark joined in by rolling in from 20 feet to win the 13th, lifting them two ahead, then cancelled out Coughlin claiming the 16th by holing a long-range birdie at the next to complete their third win of the week.

Khang's defeat was her first in 10 Solheim Cup matches and ended a six-match winning streak, one shy of the record, while Coughlin's loss was the first ever for Team USA.

"I think we really turned it on during the back nine," Grant said. "We really got our things together and started playing like we wanted to. It was a really good game - I think they were just right behind us."

Woad and Hull are the first pairing in history to play each of the first four sessions and not return at least one point, having never led during a match where Noh fired an eagle and four birdies over the front nine to reach the turn two ahead.

Europe won the opening hole of the back nine but lost the 13th to a Lee birdie, with Woad matching Lee's birdie at the 15th and finding another at the 17th before Team USA closed out another point with a final-hole par.

Nadaud won two sessions with Mimi Rhodes but was sent out in match three alongside Leona Maguire, who chipped in for eagle at the eighth and birdied the next before the Americans delivered a three-hole burst on their way to victory.

Both teams then descended to the closing holes to follow the final match, where Ciganda won back-to-back holes from the 13th before Duncan won the next and Kupcho nailed her incredible birdie at the 17th.

Another dramatic birdie at the last completed a stunning comeback and left Team USA winning the fourballs session 3-1, leaving the teams level after two days for the third consecutive Solheim Cup on European soil.

"That was huge," Team USA captain Angela Stanford said. "That absolutely turned our tide. She [Kupcho] just doesn't give up and she's a fighter. Now her team has seen that in person."

Play will begin at 11.10am local time (1010 BST) on Sunday, with heavy rain expected during most of the final-day singles. The last three Solheim Cups tied heading into the final day have resulted in European wins on home soil.

articles.title: Irish Open 2026: Inspired Shane Lowry takes four-shot lead into final round at Doonbeg
articles.summary: Shane Lowry produces an inspired display on the greens to take a four-shot lead into the final round of the Irish Open and close in on his first individual win since 2022.
articles.body:
16 S Lowry (Ire); -12 J Skov Olesen (Den); -9 J Niemann (Chi); -7 D Rodrigues (Por), T McKibbin (NI)

Selected others: -6 P Reed (US), R Fisher (Eng), R Hojgaard (Den), A Sullivan (Eng); -4 A Fitzpatrick (Eng), R MacIntyre (Sco); -2 L Nolan (Ire); -1 J Rahm (Spa); +2 R McIlroy (NI)

Shane Lowry produced an inspired display on the greens to take a four-shot lead into the final round of the Irish Open and close in on his first individual win since 2022.

The Irishman started the third round three shots clear after shooting a scintillating course-record 62 on Friday at Trump International Golf Links in Doonbeg, County Clare.

Despite being caught by Denmark's Jacob Skov Olesen, Lowry one-putted every green on the back nine in a five-under 65 to maintain control of the tournament.

"I'm normally the one watching other people do it, so why not me sometimes," Lowry said when asked about his joy on the greens.

"It's nice, I'm seeing my lines well and starting the ball where I want and they're going in and hopefully that stays that way for another 24 hours."

Olesen, chasing his first DP World Tour title, bogeyed the final hole to shoot a four-under 66, a score matched by Chile's Joaquin Niemann to move into third place on his own.

On a day when play was briefly halted amid US President Donald Trump's arrival at the course as part of a two-day visit to Ireland, defending champion Rory McIlroy (74) and two-time winner Jon Rahm (72) both slipped back to erase their hopes of lifting the trophy again.

Irish Open round three recap as Lowry shines again

Having started the round three clear, Lowry made two birdies in his opening four holes with his rhythm seemingly unaffected by a brief pause in play while he was on the third hole as Trump arrived after landing on Air Force One at Shannon Airport in County Clare.

While Lowry bogeyed the fifth, he rolled in an 11-foot putt for a birdie four on the eighth and never looked back.

The 2019 Open champion birdied 10, 13 and 15 and holed a series of crucial par putts to keep the chasing pack at bay.

Playing with Lowry, Olesen was unfazed for most of the round. The 27-year-old left-hander, who is 11th on the season-long Race to Dubai standings, birdied three and four before he drained a 31-foot putt for an eagle three at the eighth.

A birdie at nine followed, which allowed Olesen to stay in touch with Lowry until a nervy finish when he missed a nine-footer for birdie on 17 and a three-foot putt for par on the last.

Niemann, meanwhile, mixed six birdies with two bogeys to move third on his own, albeit seven shots adrift of Lowry. The 27-year-old is chasing his first DP World Tour win since 2023, but has collected nine LIV Tour victories over the past three seasons.

Northern Ireland's Tom McKibbin chipped in for birdie on the 13th to move nine under but bogeyed two of his final four holes to sit alongside Portugal's Daniel Rodrigues, who matched Lowry's 65.

Rasmus Hojgaard, who pipped McIlroy to the title at Royal County Down in 2024, finished six under having reached 10 under with five birdies in his first 10 holes.

McIlroy's challenge fades as Trump arrives

It was a day to forget for McIlroy, however, as two double bogeys on the front nine quickly dashed the six-time major winner's hopes of a surge through the field.

McIlroy, who was looking for his ball on the third hole as Air Force One flew overhead, will attend a dinner with Trump on Saturday night.

"I guess that's not the experience we're used to in a way. I think it's Air Force One's maiden voyage, so that was pretty cool," McIlroy told reporters about the president's arrival.

"Cool to sort of see all that going on. I was trying to avoid making doubles at that point, so I was trying to concentrate on my own stuff as well."

McIlroy said he hopes his friend Lowry can keep it going as he chases a first title since the 2022 BMW PGA Championship at Wentworth.

Lowry squandered chances to win in Dubai and Florida earlier this year but says he is "feeling good" as he hunts his second Irish Open title, 17 years after a memorable triumph as a 22-year-old amateur.

"Yeah, look, it's a big day for me tomorrow," he said.

"I'm going to be leading my home tournament and it would mean the world to knock this one off.

"So I'm just going to have to put my head down, get back to work whenever my tee time is tomorrow, and give it a run."

articles.title: Amgen Irish Open: Shane Lowry retains lead of home event as Donald Trump arrives despite protests
articles.summary: Shane Lowry leads by four shots heading into the weekend, clear of Denmark's Jacob Skov Olesen who carded a bogey at the last; play was delayed just before 3pm as Donald Trump's helicopter landed to allow him to watch Rory McIlroy on the 18th green
articles.body:
The home favourite delighted fans at Trump International Links in Doonbeg, on a day when the US President paid a visit to the course bearing his name.

After breaking the course record on Friday , Lowry carried on his superb form into the weekend with only Dane Jacob Skov Olesen remaining close, as he looked set to match the leader's 65 on Saturday.

But after Lowry holed out for par on 18, Olesen was unable to make his putt so carded a disappointing bogey at the last, following an excellent round.

Lowry retains the clubhouse lead at 16-under par for the tournament with Olesen four shots adrift. The next closest player is Joaquin Niemann, who led after Thursday, at nine under.

"Anytime you play a links golf in 15-20mph winds and it got a little cold at the end there, it's going to be hard and you're going to have some testers for pars," Lowry said.

"I felt like I did a great job today of just staying in the moment and playing my own game. Yeah, I had, you know, so much fun out there on the back nine.

"The crowds were incredible. They cheered me on the whole way home and hopefully will do the same tomorrow."

Donald Trump landed just in time to see Rory McIlroy hole out on 18, but the Northern Irishman had a day to forget. His 76 leaves him well out of contention heading into Sunday.

"I guess not the experience we're used to in a way," said McIlroy. "I think it's Air Force One's maiden voyage, I think, so that was pretty cool.

"Cool to sort of see all that going on. I was trying to avoid making doubles at that point so I was trying to concentrate on my own stuff as well."

Trump ignores protests across country to attend Irish Open

Thousands protested against Donald Trump's two-day visit to Ireland on Sunday, with organisers claiming a turnout in the tens of thousands in Dublin.

Sinn Féin and the Greens were among the political parties taking part, and the Irish Gardaí police force mounted a major security operation as the protest disrupted traffic and public transport in the city centre.

Smaller demonstrations were held at Shannon Airport, where the US military's use of the airport for transit and refuelling is a long-standing grievance, and in the village of Doonbeg, close to the course.

Trump had completed a series of engagements in Dublin and left the city before the main march began.

articles.title: Illustrating Chinese Brideshead Revisited was a privilege
articles.summary: Oxford-based artist Weimin He talks of being part of a "deeply immersive", yet "challenging" project.
articles.body:
"People told me they wanted to read the book after seeing my illustrations."

It took Oxford-based artist Weimin He nearly a year to create his "deeply immersive", yet "challenging" project - the first illustrations for a Chinese edition of Evelyn Waugh's Brideshead Revisited, published in August.

Having lived in the city for more than 20 years, he said it was "a privilege" to have depicted local places featured in the novel and to have researched what they were like in the 1920s and 1930s.

He said he had read the book "countless" times both in English and Chinese but had also tried to draw "from the author's perspective".

The first part of the novel follows the Oxford student life of Charles Ryder and the friendship he starts with the eccentric undergraduate Lord Sebastian Flyte.

Many Oxfordshire places are featured such as The Botanic Garden, Christ Church college and Thame.

The book was published by Shanghai Literature and Art Publishing House in a limited edition of 500 copies, for which He created 12 charcoal drawings, 12 pen-and-ink drawings and one drawing of Aloysius, Lord Sebastian's teddy bear .

"I tried to do illustrations from the author's perspective, not just from me - I try to understand what the author won't show to readers ... and also capture the atmosphere of nearly 100 years ago."

Listen to the latest news from Oxfordshire

Other sources of his inspiration were the "fantastic" 1981 TV series and the 2008 film of the same name.

The artist said he had spent most time on a bird's-eye view scene of Charles and Sebastian having a picnic.

He said to him all characters were "quite distinctive" but he liked the relationships between them the most.

"Because I live in Oxford, sometimes I meet eccentric people - [Evelyn Waugh] really depicts people so, so well."

He said the translator Zheng Haiyao, who uses the pen name Kaiti, had initially highlighted about 50 paragraphs for him.

He also chose a moment from the epilogue, when an older Charles Ryder converts to Catholicism.

"That part really touched me, I thought that description [is] the soul of the book," He said.

"It took me a long time to find the right image because the TV series just showed Charles praying and I thought that's something a bit too obvious."

He, who became an artist-in-residence at Green Templeton College in 2018, said he knew the city "very well", as he had "never lived in any other place for so long, even in China".

"The very route I cycle daily into town was the same road Charles and Sebastian drove in their vintage car to the countryside."

He said he would not depict the "really familiar" places mentioned in the book such as the Botley Road, High Street and Broad Street.

"I feel it's something really already inside of me, but for Chinese readers, maybe there's something new."

The artist said he had searched for "vast numbers" of images from the 1920s and 1930s online, hoping to "get as close as possible to the Oxford of that era".

"The translation [is] just excellent and is being welcomed in China."

One comment on his Instagram post reads "Seeing your illustrations makes me feel like reading this book".

"And this really is the best comment I've ever received," He said.

articles.title: Carlota Ciganda y Julia López iluminan la reconquista europea de la Solheim Cup
articles.standfirst: Las españolas ganaron sus partidos y Europa recupera por 15-12 el título dos años después
articles.summary: Las españolas ganaron sus partidos y Europa recupera por 15-12 el título dos años después
articles.body: Europa vuelve a reinar en la Solheim Cup. Lo ha hecho en Bernardus Golf después de un domingo que comenzó bajo un auténtico diluvio y terminó con el cielo abriéndose y el marcador teñido de azul (15-12), con las españolas Carlota Ciganda y Julia López Ramírez poniendo un marcado acento español a la reconquista. Dos generaciones distintas, una veterana que volvió a agigantarse cuando más pesaba la competición y una debutante que se marcha invicta y convertida en el alma de la fiesta del equipo de Anna Nordqvist. El privilegio de desatar definitivamente la euforia, sin embargo, correspondió a otra debutante, Lottie Woad. Y pocas jugadoras podían merecer un desenlace semejante después de lo sufrido durante toda la semana. La inglesa, llamada a escribir muchas páginas de la historia del golf europeo, había disputado junto a Charley Hull las cuatro sesiones por parejas con mucho menos premio del que había merecido su juego. Un empate y tres derrotas que llegaron incluso a hacerle sentir, según confesó después, que estaba fallando a sus compañeras. Nordqvist se encargó de levantarle el ánimo. Le recordó que sus estadísticas de birdies estaban entre las mejores de la semana y que simplemente tenía que seguir confiando en su golf. Y el destino le reservó el mejor premio. Woad llegó a colocarse cuatro arriba frente a Auston Kim, vio cómo la estadounidense le ganaba tres hoyos consecutivos del 12 al 14 y, cuando el partido amenazaba con complicarse, recuperó el control. Ganó el 16 y en el 17 contempló cómo el birdie de Kim para prolongar el duelo se escapaba por muy poco. Victoria por 2&1 y Europa en 14 puntos. Con Carlota teniendo ya asegurado al menos medio punto en su partido frente a Jennifer Kupcho, la Copa era matemáticamente europea. Lo curioso es que Woad ni siquiera lo sabía. "Pensaba que el partido de Carlota era el que decidiría la victoria", reconoció instantes después. "Al final resultó que conseguí el putt ganador". Un final extraordinario para quien había llegado al domingo sintiendo que no estaba aportando lo suficiente. La jornada había empezado precisamente con la otra integrante de aquella castigada pareja. Nordqvist colocó a Hull en cabeza y la inglesa respondió. Se adelantó en el primer hoyo frente a Megan Khang y no volvió a mirar atrás. Khang, hasta entonces invicta en sus cuatro individuales de Solheim, no consiguió ganar un solo hoyo y Hull se impuso por 3&2. Las dos jugadoras que durante viernes y sábado habían sufrido juntas, terminaron separadas abriendo y cerrando el camino de Europa hacia el título. Entre ellas, Bernardus vivió durante horas una auténtica marea azul. Linn Grant culminó una semana sensacional derrotando por 4&3 a Angel Yin para completar un impecable cuatro de cuatro. La sueca volvió a alimentarse de un público al que definió después como el "jugador número 13" de Europa. Nanna Koerstz Madsen, que había pasado todo el sábado fuera del equipo después de sus problemas del viernes, encontró también su redención con un 2&1 frente a Allisen Corpuz. Y qué decir de Nastasia Nadaud. La debutante francesa, que apenas unos meses atrás ni siquiera imaginaba que estaría jugando una Solheim Cup, superó por 3&2 a Andrea Lee para sumar su tercer punto de la semana. Una actuación formidable para una jugadora que, junto a Mimi Rhodes, se convirtió en uno de los grandes descubrimientos europeos de Bernardus. Estados Unidos se resistía a entregar la Solheim. Nelly Korda impuso la ley de la número uno del mundo ante Rhodes con un contundente 4&2, mientras Alison Lee protagonizaba una de las remontadas de la semana. Llegó cuatro abajo frente a Esther Henseleit después del 11 y ganó cinco de los seis hoyos siguientes para imponerse por uno arriba. Un triunfo que le permitió completar un extraordinario cuatro de cuatro en la semana. Más tarde, Lauren Coughlin añadió otro punto estadounidense derrotando por 2&1 a Leona Maguire. Pero para entonces Europa había encontrado otra protagonista inesperada. Julia López Ramírez llegó a Bernardus como debutante y se marcha sin conocer la derrota. Nordqvist sólo la utilizó en dos partidos, pero aprovechó ambos: empató el viernes junto a Carlota frente a Korda y Coughlin y derrotó este domingo por 3&2 a Yealimi Noh. Punto y medio de dos posibles. Su desenlace ante Noh fue una de las grandes imágenes del domingo. Julia llegó dos arriba al 16, alcanzó el green del par 5 de dos golpes y terminó embocando el birdie que cerraba su victoria. Levantó los brazos y las compañeras que ya habían terminado sus partidos corrieron hacia ella para abrazarla. La recién llegada había conquistado al vestuario. "Ha sido el putt más importante de mi carrera", aseguró después. Había perdido incluso la voz de tanto gritar durante una semana en la que, como ella misma explicó, dejó de jugar para sí misma para hacerlo por el equipo. Y quedaba Carlota. Siempre Carlota. Tres años después de convertirse en la heroína de Finca Cortesín con el punto que permitió a Europa retener la Copa frente a Nelly Korda, la navarra volvió a encontrarse en el centro de la escena. Y esta vez había una cuenta pendiente... Menos de 24 horas antes, Kupcho le había infligido uno de esos golpes que dejan cicatriz. Carlota y Céline Boutier parecían tener encarrilado su fourball del sábado hasta que la estadounidense embocó un putt imposible de 91 pies, casi 28 metros, en el 17. Y todavía tuvo fuerzas para firmar otro birdie desde larga distancia en el 18 que entregó la victoria a Estados Unidos y dejó la Solheim empatada 8-8. Boutier terminó entre lágrimas y Europa se marchó tocada. Hasta José María Olazábal intervino desde la distancia enviando un mensaje a Ciganda que, según contó Laura Davies, ayudó a levantar el ánimo del equipo. El sorteo quiso que Carlota tuviera delante precisamente a Kupcho en los individuales. Y salió disparada. Después de empatar el primero, ganó cuatro hoyos consecutivos para colocarse cuatro arriba después del 5. La estadounidense reaccionó, pero cada vez que amenazó seriamente con regresar apareció la navarra. Especialmente memorable fue su birdie desde unos 14 metros en el 7, inmediatamente después de haber perdido el hoyo anterior. Kupcho consiguió estrechar de nuevo el partido, pero Carlota volvió a abrir una brecha de tres hoyos y llegó al 16 en posición inmejorable para completar su particular revancha. La estadounidense había tenido la última palabra el sábado. Carlota se la reservó para el domingo. "Hemos tenido un equipo fantástico, uno de los mejores de los últimos años, y estoy feliz de que hayamos ganado por nuestra capitana", reconoció la española. "No sé qué pasa en la Solheim, pero emboco muchísimos putts. ¡Tengo que llevarme esta mentalidad al resto de torneos!", añadió eufórica. Y todo ocurrió en una jornada de golf extrema. Durante buena parte de la mañana cayó tanta agua sobre Bernardus que mantener secos guantes, grips y palos se convirtió casi en otra parte del juego. Los greenes perdieron velocidad, las distancias cambiaron y el campo pasó a exigir paciencia y precisión más que una sucesión de birdies. Europa construyó bajo aquel diluvio buena parte de su ventaja. Horas después dejó de llover, apareció el sol y Estados Unidos encontró cierta reacción. Alison Lee llegó incluso a reconocer que el cambio meteorológico había acompañado al de su propio juego. No fue suficiente. Europa había llegado al domingo empatada 8-8 y necesitaba ganar los individuales porque un 14-14 habría permitido a Estados Unidos conservar el trofeo. Nordqvist había repetido durante la semana que su equipo estaba "en una misión". La completó en un domingo en el que muchas de sus cuestionadas decisiones terminaron encontrando respuesta: Hull abrió el camino, Grant completó una semana perfecta, Madsen respondió después de descansar todo el sábado, las debutantes dieron puntos decisivos y Woad, a quien la capitana había tenido que devolver la confianza, terminó protagonizando el instante de la victoria. Bernardus amaneció bajo un diluvio y terminó celebrando bajo un cielo azul con una imagen espectacular: todas las jugadoras de Nordqvist abrazadas, recorriendo la calle del 18 para acompañar a Boutier en el último partido del día, que ya no importaba. Europa recuperó la Solheim Cup. La de Nordqvist, la de Hull y Woad, la de una generación de debutantes que apunta muy alto. Y por supuesto, la de Julia, que llegó casi de puntillas y se marcha invicta y abrazada por todas sus compañeras. Y la de Carlota. Otra vez Carlota. Una leyenda del golf europeo que ha vuelto a demostrar su enorme talento, compromiso y liderazgo incluso cuando más difíciles parecían ponerse las cosas.

articles.title: Solheim Cup 2026:  Europe's win over United States fuelled by Hull, Woad and Ciganda
articles.summary: Charley Hull gets the ball rolling as Europe's big guns finally came to the fore in Sunday's singles as they wrestled the Solheim Cup back from the United States with a 15½-12½ victory at Bernardus Golf Club in the Netherlands.
articles.body:
Charley Hull got the ball rolling as Europe's big names finally came to the fore in Sunday's singles as they wrestled the Solheim Cup back from the United States with a 15-13 victory at Bernardus Golf Club in the Netherlands.

Hull, who had garnered just half a point across the first two days in an unprofitable partnership with fellow Englishwoman Lottie Woad, led Europe out again on Sunday and claimed a 3&2 win over American livewire Megan Khang.

It delivered an immediate boost to Anna Nordqvist's team in the singles format that they have been unbeaten in since their last home defeat in 2015.

Woad, who alongside Hull is ranked among the top 10 players in the world, also delivered, with her 2&1 win over fellow debutant Auston Kim sparking wild celebrations on the 17th green.

With Carlota Ciganda three holes up heading on to the 16th, it assured the hosts of reaching the 14½-point tally required to triumph in the biggest team competition in women's golf.

"It was the no-brainer to put Charley first," said Nordqvist.

"We saw the stats and Charley and Lottie were actually top-four players that made the most birdies for the week. They just played really tough matches.

"People don't understand how good all these players are and how good the golf has been in the past three days.

"So Charley was a no-brainer, and then finishing strong with Carlota. As we know, she's done it in the past."

Any question marks over Nordqvist's captaincy had revolved around repeatedly pairing her two star English players together over the first two days.

And Hull was one of the first on the scene to congratulate Woad, with the quip, "finally got our points didn't we Lottie".

Veteran Ciganda carrying her side over the winning line in the penultimate match against Jennifer Kupcho could not have been more fitting.

On Saturday evening Kupcho had hushed the crowd and yelled "vamos" as she drained a 91-foot putt on the 17th and then knocked in a 30-footer on the 18th green to steal a point from the Spaniard in the fourballs.

It felt like a moment that had turned the momentum of the match towards Angela Stanford's team but fewer then 24 hours later, Kupcho and her US team-mates had little to cheer with all the euphoria draped around those wearing blue and yellow.

Having started the day level at 8-8, Europe's quartet of rookies deserve huge credit.

Having impressed in the foursomes and fourballs, Spain's Julia Lopez Ramirez and France's Nastasia Nadaud once again demonstrated their suitability for the biggest of stages.

Lopez Ramirez defeated Yealimi Noh 3&2, while Nadaud always looked in control against Andrea Lee to win by the same scoreline.

Mimi Rhodes, who had partnered Nadaud to two victories, was only downed by a superb performance from world number one Nelly Korda, while Lauren Coughlin, Lindy Duncan, Alison Lee were the only others to put intermittent splashes of red on Sunday's scoreboard.

Coughlin, who had already earned two-and-a-half points this week, ended Leona Maguire's unbeaten singles record.

Duncan beat Maja Stark, while Alison Lee came from four holes down to complete the biggest singles comeback in the history of the Solheim Cup, with a 1UP success over Esther Henseleit.

But it was simply not enough for the visitors, whose wait for a first win on European soil since 2015 continues.

"The Europeans played great today, and that's the way it goes," said Stanford.

"Their backs were against the wall, they had nothing to lose, and that's exactly what they did, they came out and played well."

By the time Rose Zhang concluded her 2UP win against Celine Boutier in the last match on the course, the European party was in full swing.

articles.title: Solheim Cup 2026: Team Europe regain trophy from Team USA after Lottie Woad, Carlota Ciganda close out thrilling home win
articles.summary: Lottie Woad took Team Europe to 14 points before Carlota Ciganda confirmed a home victory over Team USA at Bernardus Golf; Anna Nordqvist's side regained the trophy with a 15-13 win on a rainy final day in the Netherlands
articles.body:
Europe went into a rainy Sunday at Bernardus Golf tied 8-8 and requiring at least 6.5 points for victory, two years on from losing to Team USA, with Charley Hull leading from the front to beat Megan Khang 3&2 and put early blue on the board.

Anna Nordqvist's side briefly led in eight of the 12 matches and moved further ahead when Linn Grant beat Angel Yin, completing her perfect week, but Alison Lee gave Team USA hope with a record comeback from four down to beat Esther Henseleit 1up.

World No 1 Nelly Korda levelled the contest when she saw off rookie Mimi Rhodes 4&3, but wins for Nastasia Nadaud, Nanna Koerstz Madsen and Julia Lopez Ramirez moved Europe closer to victory.

Lottie Woad beat Auston Kim to take the hosts to 14 points and sparked European celebrations, with Ciganda guaranteed at least a half-point, before the veteran - whose singles win 2023 saw them retain in Spain - defeated Jennifer Kupcho to confirm home victory.

How Team Europe claimed Europe on Solheim Cup glory

Kupcho's sensational late birdies on Saturday evening had left Team USA captain Angela Stanford feeling like they had 'turned the tide' in their favour, only for Team Europe to quickly take charge on the final day.

Hull thrashed Korda 6&4 in the singles two years and was trusted to lead out Europe again, despite registering 0.5 points with Woad over the first four sessions, with the Englishwoman validating Nordqvist's decision by claiming a full point.

The eight-time Solheim Cup player won the opening hole with the par and never trailed against Khang, with Hull matching the American's birdie at the eighth and then winning both par-fives on the back nine to close out victory.

"I've been giving myself so many chances, so that's been quite frustrating," Hull admitted. "Obviously didn't hole a lot today, but I was just very steady, hit a lot of greens."

Grant became just the ninth player in history to post a 4-0-0 record or after a dominant 4&3 win over Yin, with American Lee matching the Swede's record by coming back from four down with seven holes to stun Henseleit in match two.

" I just did my best to stay consistent," Lee said. "That front nine was pretty tough with the rain coming down. I couldn't give myself birdie chances and put myself in a good spot. Thankfully the weather turned around, and my golf game did as well."

Korda produced her performance of the week against Rhodes but Europe's other three rookies all returned points, with Nadaud seeing off Andrea Lee 3&2 for a third win of her debut before Lopez Ramirez capped off an unbeaten debut by beating Yealimi Noh.

Madsen had seen off Allisen Corpuz before Woad recovered from losing three consecutive holes on the back nine to beat Kim and leave Europe on the brink, after a brief period of Team USA momentum, while Ciganda quickly built an early lead against Kupcho and claimed the winning point.

"I'm so happy," Ciganda said. "I think we had a great team all week. I think it's been one of the best teams that we've had in the last few years."

Team USA rookie Lindy Duncan ended Maja Stark's perfect record and Lauren Coughlin inflicted Leona Maguire's first ever Solheim singles defeat, reducing the winning margin, while Rose Zhang beat Celine Boutier 2up in the bottom match to leave the Frenchwoman without a point for her week.

Nordqvist savours 'amazing' win as Stanford praises Europe

"There's just been so much hard work this week and in the last two years leading up to this from not only me, but all the background team. The helpers have been amazing this week, making it easy for the players just to play.

"We just had a really good vibe all week. Everyone's been really good team-mates. We talked a lot about the fast starts this week with the way the golf course was. I'm just really, really proud of the players for starting strong and even finishing strong."

"I think that we did a lot of things right leading up to it and I know we did. They fought hard and we seemed to always be on the same page.

"The Europeans played great today and that's the way it goes. Their backs were against the wall, they had nothing to lose, and that's exactly what they did. They came out and played well, so good for them."

The Ladies European Tour heads to Spain next for La Sella Open, beginning Thursday and held at La Sella Golf Resort, while the LPGA Tour takes a week off before the Walmart N Arkansas Championship from September 25-27.

articles.title: Amgen Irish Open: Shane Lowry secures record 11-stroke victory at Trump International Links in Doonbeg
articles.summary: Shane Lowry cards eight birdies in final-round 63, including one at the 18th to sign off his stunning triumph in style; Rory McIlory defiant, saying "I don't feel too far away" after signing off disappointing title defence with a round of 67 to finish one under
articles.body:
It's Lowry's seventh career title and his second Irish Open triumph, following his 2009 victory as a 22-year-old amateur, with US President Donald Trump presenting him with the trophy.

It's a welcome return to the winner's circle for Lowry after a series of agonising near-misses earlier this season, including a double-bogey on the final hole that cost him the Dubai Invitational by two strokes and a collapse at the Cognizant Classic, where he surrendered a three-stroke lead with three holes to play by closing with two double-bogeys.

The result was never in doubt at Trump International Golf Links in Doonbeg, however, as Lowry - holding a four-shot lead heading into Sunday - extended his advantage with a superb final round, while Trump watched on for the second consecutive day.

Crowds cheered Donald Trump and chanted "USA" as he told them he was removing tariffs from Irish whiskey, saying he had discussed the matter with Taoiseach Micheal Martin, minister for sport, who was also on the 18th green for the prizegiving ceremony, along with Charlie McConalogue, minister for state.

Lowry hails 'spectacular week' | 'I can't wait to bring trophy home'

Lowry carded eight birdies for his round and just one bogey, at the ninth, with a pair of stunning 45-foot putts at the par-three seventh and par-four 15th sending the watching crowd into a frenzy. He capped his victory in style with another long-range birdie at the last.

"This year has been quite difficult on the course for me," an emotional Lowry said after his triumph. "I've had a few chances to win, and there's been some really tough times.

"To come here this week and do this, I don't do things by half measures! I can't believe I'm standing here with that leaderboard.

"This has been the most spectacular week. It has been unreal.

"When things are not going well at this level, it's hard at home as well, but my wife's been a huge support, and my kids. I just love them so much and I'm so happy for them. I can't wait to bring a trophy home.

"My daughter is always ask me when you're going to bring a trophy home. So, yes, I'm going to bring one home."

Lowry had taken such a sizeable advantage into Sunday in large part thanks to breaking the course record with a second-round 62 on Friday

Jacob Skov Olesen, Lowry's closest challenger at 12 under and four shots back overnight, slipped down the leaderboard with a three-over 73. Patrick Reed's closing 64 and Rasmus Neergaard-Petersen's 63 were impressive enough to earn them second and third respectively, but Lowry had already surged clear.

Joaquin Niemann took a share of second with Reed on 12 under, with Neergaard-Petersen one back.

England's Alex Fitzpatrick was tied-seventh at nine under, a closing 64 from Sergio Garcia had him six under, on the same score as Robert MacIntyre and Matt Wallace, among others.

Jon Rahm finished four under and reigning champion Rory McIlroy rounded off a disappointing week with his best round of 67 to end his title defence one under.

McIlroy positive despite disappointing defence: 'I don't feel too far away'

McIlroy said his final round has given him some encouragement to take into next week at the BMW Championship at Wentworth, a tournament he won in 2014 and has been runner-up at three times since.

"I've seen enough good stuff this week to give me encouragement going into next week," McIlroy said. "It's a golf course that I know well and one I've had success on.

"Obviously this wasn't the week that I wanted but, at the same time, I don't feel too far away and I feel good going into Wentworth.

"I thought I hit the ball pretty well for the most part. A couple of bad decisions off the tees yesterday but, overall, my iron play was a lot better, my wedge play was pretty good for the most part and obviously it was a struggle on the greens.

"That was the difficult thing and why I wasn't able to get myself into contention. I need a little bit of time on the putting green the next couple days and to get familiar with the greens at Wentworth again."

The DP World Tour heads to Wentworth in Surrey next for the BMW PGA Championship.

articles.title: Irish Open: 'I can't believe it' - Shane Lowry powers to record win at Doonbeg
articles.summary: Shane Lowry produces a frontrunning masterclass to cruise to a record 11-shot win at the Irish Open and end his four-year wait for an individual title in emphatic style.
articles.body:
23 S Lowry (Ire); -12 P Reed (US), J Niemann (Chi); -11 R Neergaard-Petersen (Den); -10 T McKibbin (NI), G De Leo (Ita)

Selected others: -9 A Fitzpatrick (Eng), J Skov Olesen (Den); -8 E Ferguson (Sco); -7 P Waring (Eng); -6 S Garcia (Spa), M Wallace (Eng), R MacIntyre (Sco); -4 J Rahm (Spa), D Law (Sco), R Fisher (Eng); -3 L Nolan (Ire); -1 R McIlroy (NI), +2 B Koepka (US).

Shane Lowry produced a frontrunning masterclass to clinch a record 11-shot win at the Irish Open and end his four-year wait for an individual title in emphatic style.

The 39-year-old Irishman, who entered the final round four strokes clear of Jacob Skov Olesen, carded a seven-under 63 to win his national open for the second time - 17 years after his first - amid joyous scenes at Trump International Golf Links in Doonbeg, County Clare.

Under the watchful gaze of visiting US President Donald Trump - who presented him with the trophy - and roared home by thousands of fans, Lowry mixed eight birdies and one bogey to canter to his first title since September 2022.

Having squandered chances to win in Dubai and Florida earlier this year, Lowry was a study in intensity and focus until the emotion poured out of him after he sunk a 29-foot birdie putt on the final green.

"This year has been quite difficult on the course for me," said the 2019 Open champion.

"I had a few chances to win. To come here this week and do this, I don't know, I just don't do things like half-measures."

Lowry shot 67-62-65-63 for a tournament record score of 257, while American Patrick Reed and Chile's Joaquin Niemann shared second place on 12 under.

Irish Open: Recap as Dominant Lowry cruises to 11-shot win at Doonbeg

Lowry - who posted a course-record 62 to seize control of the tournament on Friday - stumbled down the stretch earlier this year while chasing wins at the Dubai Invitational and Cognizant Classic in Florida.

He also collapsed to an eight-over 80 in the final round of the Masters having trailed eventual winner Rory McIlroy by just two shots entering the final day, which he highlighted as an especially difficult experience during his post-victory remarks at Doonbeg.

On Sunday, however, he never gave the chasing pack hope as he birdied four of his first eight holes to reach 20 under, with a holed 43-footer for a birdie two on the seventh undoubtedly the highlight.

While he stumbled momentarily with a bogey on nine, he bounced right back on the next and birdied 14 before sinking another monster putt on 15.

Having nearly chipped in for another unlikely birdie on 16, Lowry parred the next before drawing one last roar from the crowd when he poured in a 29-footer on the final hole.

"A lot of things have went right for me but this has been the most spectacular week," added Lowry, who savoured another win on home soil after watching Irish boxer Katie Taylor win her farewell fight at Dublin's Croke Park last week.

"It's just mad. I can't believe it. My mum was just standing there. I have my wife and my kids back in Florida.

"When things are not going well at this level, it's hard at home as well but my wife has been a huge support and my kids, I love them so much. I'm so happy for them.

"I can't wait to bring a trophy home. My daughter is always asking, 'when are you going to bring a trophy home?', so I'm going to bring a trophy home."

McKibbin in top five as McIlroy looks to Wentworth

Denmark's Rasmus Neergaard-Petersen matched Lowry's 63 to finish fourth, while Northern Ireland's Tom McKibbin shot 67 to secure a top-five finish.

England's Alex Fitzpatrick (65) and Scotland's Ewen Ferguson (64) also finished strongly to seal top-10 finishes, while 2025 winner Rory McIlroy closed with a 67 to finish a disappointing week in a tie for 41st, 22 shots adrift of Lowry.

Reed's tie for second will also widen his lead over McIlroy at the top of the season-long Race to Dubai rankings.

However, six-time major winner McIlroy insisted he was reasonably satisfied with his game heading into the BMW PGA Championship at Wentworth, which begins on Thursday.

"I think overall, I've seen enough good stuff this week to give me encouragement going into next week, a golf course that I know well and a golf course that I've had success on," said McIlroy, who tumbled down the leaderboard with a 74 on Saturday.

"[It] obviously wasn't the week that I wanted but at the same time, I don't feel too far away, and I feel good about going into Wentworth next week."

articles.standfirst: El irlandés ganó en 2009 como amateur; hoy arrasa con 23 bajo par y 11 golpes de ventaja
articles.summary: El irlandés ganó en 2009 como amateur; hoy arrasa con 23 bajo par y 11 golpes de ventaja
articles.body: Shane Lowry (-23) tenía 22 años y todavía era amateur cuando en 2009 sorprendió al mundo del golf conquistando el Amgen Irish Open. Diecisiete años después, convertido en campeón del Open y en una de las grandes figuras del golf europeo, el irlandés volvió a levantar el trofeo de su país. Y esta vez lo hizo sin dejar espacio para la emoción: ganó en Doonbeg con once golpes de ventaja sobre Patrick Reed (-12) y Joaquin Niemann (-12). Lowry llegó al domingo con cuatro golpes de margen y, lejos de limitarse a administrar su renta, volvió a pisar el acelerador. Hizo ocho birdies, en los hoyos 1, 5, 7, 8, 10, 14, 15 y 18, por un único bogey en el 9, para despedirse con un extraordinario 63, siete bajo par, a uno del 62 con el que puso tierra de por medio el viernes haciendo récord del campo. El birdie final puso el broche a una semana espectacular de 67, el tremendo 62, 65 y 63 golpes, para un acumulado de 257. La mejor noticia española llegó de la mano de Sergio García (-6). El castellonense, que había comenzado el torneo con un 75 que lo dejó contra las cuerdas, cerró su participación con un magnífico 64, seis bajo par en el día, que le permitió escalar hasta la 14ª posición. Después de su complicado estreno, sus tres últimas tarjetas fueron 65, para pasar el corte, 70 y 64, una notable reacción que le permitió terminar como el mejor español de la semana. También terminó con un seis menos el canario Rafa Cabrera Bello (-4), que compartió la 23ª plaza con Jon Rahm (-4). El de Barrika volvió a bajar de 70 golpes con un 67, pero nunca pudo acercarse a una cabeza que Lowry había dejado demasiado lejos. El golfista vasco cerró así el torneo con tarjetas de 70, 67, 72 y 67, muy lejos de poder pelear por esa tercera victoria en el Irish Open que le habría permitido igualar a Seve Ballesteros. Eugenio Chacarra (-2), con 66, fue el siguiente español en la clasificación, mientras que Ángel Hidalgo (+2) terminó con 68, Pablo Larrazábal (+2) con 71 y Alejandro del Rey (+4) también con 71. Todos quedaron eclipsados por el gran protagonista de la semana. Lowry había ganado el Irish Open una vez, cuando todavía jugaba sin cobrar un euro de premio. Diecisiete años después volvió a hacerlo, ya como profesional y ante su público, con una superioridad aplastante.

articles.title: Solheim Cup 2026: Anna Nordqvist savours Team Europe win and explains 'no-brainer' call to put Charley Hull out first
articles.summary: Charley Hull went out first for Team Europe in the Solheim Cup Sunday singles, beating Megan Khang 3&2 as Anna Nordqvist's side claimed a 15-13 over Team USA at Bernardus Golf; Nordqvist paired Hull with Lottie Woad for each of the first four sessions
articles.body:
Europe regained the trophy after an exciting final day at a rainy Bernardus Golf, where Nordqvist's side won seven of the 12 points available to claim a 15-13 win over Team USA.

The visitors felt they had 'turned the tide' in their favour after a sensational finish the previous evening, where Jennifer Kupcho's sensational late birdies levelled the biennial contest, but Europe bounced back to earn a first outright win since 2021.

"This [winning] feels so good!" Nordqvist told Sky Sports . "There's just been so much hard work this week and in the last two years leading up to this from not only me, but all the background team.

"The helpers have been amazing this week, making it easy for the players just to play, and we just had a really good vibe all week. Everyone's been really good team-mates.

"Leaving the course yesterday, we were really excited for coming here today and, wow, was I impressed with every single player and caddie showing up to that first tee ready to play.

" It just seemed to be a lot of blue early on the board. We talked a lot about the fast starts this week with the way the golf course was and I'm just really, really proud of the players for starting strong and even finishing strong."

Hull thrashed Korda 6&4 in the singles two years and was trusted to lead out Europe again, despite registering 0.5 points with Lottie Woad over the first four sessions, with the Englishwoman validating Nordqvist's decision by claiming a full point.

"This was the no-brainer to put Charley [Hull] first," Nordqvist added. "We saw the stats yesterday, and Charley and Lottie [Woad] were actually top-four players that made the most birdies for the week.

"Hadn't scored really many points, but they just played really tough matches. People don't understand how good all these players are and how good the golf has been all day in the last three days."

Hull and Woad deliver after 'frustrating' week

The English duo were in danger of becoming the first players in Solheim Cup history to participate in five sessions and not have any wins, with their defeats including one by a record-equalling margin of 6&5 in the Saturday foursomes.

Hull never trailed during her 3&2 victory over Megan Khang, her first full point of the week, with Europe winning six out of the first eight singles matches for the first time in their history to close towards victory.

"I've been giving myself so many chances, so that's been quite frustrating," Hull admitted. "Obviously didn't hole a lot today, but I was just very steady, hit a lot of greens. The weather was pretty bad, so I just kept in there.

"I spoke to Mel [Reid, vice-captain] and she was like 'you know that you're the third player on both teams who have made the most birdies this week. You've just come against Yealimi Noh, who literally holed everything the last few days!'

"To be fair, we were playing well, we just weren't holing enough putts. I think that's match play for you. I'm happy that I've got a point this week, even though it's only one and a half points that I got, but it's better than none!"

Woad also claimed her first Solheim victory by beating Auston Kim and moving the hosts to 14 points, sparking wild European celebrations, before Carlota Ciganda defeated Jennifer Kupcho to confirm home victory.

"It [winning] was really important," Woad said. "I was pretty disappointed. Felt like I was playing good golf and not getting the points and felt like I was kind of letting everyone down.

"Then the captains kind of spoke to me and said the stat that I was third on birdies, so I was playing good golf and just had to trust that. That's golf sometimes - ends up I got the winning putt."

articles.title: Solheim Cup 2026: Europe captain Anna Nordqvist dismisses USA captain Angela Stanford's 'dig' at course set-up
articles.summary: Team Europe captain Anna Nordqvist defended the Solheim Cup course set-up after suggestions from Team USA that the greens had been deliberately slowed down; the home side regained the trophy with a 15-13 win after prevailing in Sunday's singles at Bernardus Golf
articles.body:
Nordqvist's side completed a 15-13 victory over Team USA after prevailing in Sunday's singles in the Netherlands.

The scores were tied at 8-8 following the opening two days, but USA captain Angela Stanford felt her side had been at a disadvantage throughout the tournament due to the slowness of the greens.

Stanford said at her post-tournament press conference: "Europe played well. I don't think we played bad. I think we just didn't make enough putts.

"And if you listen to everything I've ever said, Europeans always putt better. I don't know why. I still don't know why. I mean, I have a good idea, but I'm not going to say it right now.

"Apparently I didn't get to know the superintendent [grounds manager] as well as I should have."

When pressed further about whether she was referring to the green speeds being different to what she had been expecting, Stanford added: "Even when we showed up in July here, they were faster.

"And I don't think it had anything to do with the rain either. Now, saying that, it's my responsibility to get the team ready.

"So I'm a little frustrated with myself that I didn't drive that point home."

Nordqvist was a little surprised by the apparent dig at the greens when it was put to her at her own press conference.

"We're in Europe and in September. We know how the weather can be," she said.

"I'm not sure I believe a lot in setting up a way to fit Europe because these girls play the same golf courses week-in and week-out competing.

"We came here in July, it was a very hot and dry summer, so the course played a little bit different then.

"So if anything it was just really trying to manage firmness. But then it's obviously been raining a lot in the past couple weeks and then this week we saw a lot of rain.

"So if anything they were probably just playing a little bit softer than we all thought coming here. But that's obviously the weather, we can't control that."

The Americans were pictured celebrating on Saturday evening after Jennifer Kupcho had sunk two brilliant putts to snatch a late victory for the visitors and level the match at 8-8 rather than going into the final day trailing 9-7.

But Stanford dismissed suggestions they had reached an emotional high too early.

"That's kind of tricky because you don't ever want to take away from that moment," she said.

"The worst thing I could have done is go in there and be like, 'okay, y'all. Come off this high'. So you don't want to take away from those moments.

"We're never going to see anything like that again. I think they handled it very well.

"But I talked to Kupcho and everybody and they're like, 'yeah, we got good rest but, yeah, it did take a minute to come off because it was a pretty high high'."
